message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 140, "amount_cents": 13659}, {"order_id": 144, "amount_cents": 19464}, {"order_id": 145, "amount_cents": 9501}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll pull the refunds list and compare it with the handoff.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly: same order IDs and amounts. Next I'll pull the orders so I can identify the customers and check that the refunds line up with them.
The refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is below its order amount, so nothing looks wrong. I'll get acme's net balance from the ledger before recording any payout.
acme's net balance of 31766 matches my check: orders 140 and 143 total 45425, less the 13659 refund on order 140. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
birch's net balance of 35795 matches my check: orders 141 and 144 total 55259, less the 19464 refund on order 144. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get their net balance.

Cobalt's net of 11416 matches my check: orders 142 and 145 total 20917, less the 9501 refund on order 145. All three balances match, so Alpha's refund work checks out. I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
acme's payout of 31766 is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 35795, which matches the net balance I verified against the orders and refunds.
Birch's payout of 35795 is recorded. The last customer is cobalt, whose net balance of 11416 I already checked against orders 142 and 145 and refund 145, so I'll record that payout.
All three payouts are recorded. Each net balance matches orders minus refunds: acme 45425-13659=31766, birch 55259-19464=35795, cobalt 20917-9501=11416.
